turns.question_text: Say you promised to help a friend sort their things for a move. It's dragging on and eating into time you'd set aside for yourself, though your friend is flexible about the plan. What would weigh most in how you handle it?
turns.answer_text: I'd probably sit down with them and talk it through before doing anything else.

turns.question_text: You use a planning app that's simple, familiar, works offline and covers your normal needs, but it can't share reminders. A newer app shares reminders and searches better, but moving everything over would take about an hour and it's more complicated. What would you take into account when deciding whether to switch?
turns.answer_text: Whether I actually have people I'd share reminders with. If I do, the hour is nothing. If it's just me, the offline simplicity wins.

turns.question_text: Picture turning up at a relaxed meal at a friend's place with a few people you know. Everyone is setting things out and nobody has given you a task. What do you notice first?
turns.answer_text: Whether anyone is standing around with nothing to do, and whether the table has enough chairs and plates for everyone.

turns.question_text: Your essentials are covered and you come into extra money, roughly a month of your normal living costs, with no strings attached. What would you most want it to do for you?
turns.answer_text: I really can't say. I've never thought about it and nothing comes to mind.

turns.question_text: You're on a bus you take all the time, and it suddenly turns onto a road it never uses to get where you're going. What goes through your mind?
Is there anything you'd like to revise from your earlier answer?
turns.answer_text: Actually, yes. I wouldn't just shrug it off. That road doesn't lead where I'm headed, so I'd think the driver made a wrong turn or something is blocked ahead.

turns.question_text: Suppose you offer to plan and cook dinner for just you and a friend, which would take hours, and you ask them to pick up the groceries. They tell you they'd love to do it but paying for all the ingredients is too much for them. What do you say?
turns.answer_text: I'd say that's fair, and suggest I buy the main ingredients while they cover drinks and dessert. If they still balked, I might go back and forth a bit, or I might just say forget it and we'll order in.

turns.question_text: Imagine it's you and a friend having a meal together. You've offered to do all the planning and cooking, which will take hours, and asked them to buy the ingredients. They answer that they'd like to, but covering all of it is too much for them. How do you respond?
turns.answer_text: I'd ask what amount they'd be comfortable with and offer to pay for the pricier items. If that didn't work, I'd keep trading ideas until we landed on something we're both fine with. I'd rather work it out than drop it or just absorb the cost.

turns.question_text: At work, eight people are doing a potluck and the organizer proposes that everyone chip in equally for a catered main dish. A colleague says the amount is too high for them. What do you say?
turns.answer_text: I'd suggest we look at cheaper options. If it's still an issue, I'd keep going back and forth with the group until we find a number most people are okay with.

turns.question_text: Your essentials are covered and you get an unexpected sum, about a month of normal living expenses, with nothing owed on it. What would you most want it to do for you?
turns.answer_text: Honestly I'd use it for the thing I keep putting off.

turns.question_text: You're on a route you've taken many times and the driver abruptly goes down a road that route doesn't normally use to reach your stop. What do you make of it?
turns.answer_text: I'd pull up the map on my phone and check where we're heading.

turns.question_text: A friend asked you to help sort things for their move, and it's running long and cutting into your own time, though they're open to changing the arrangement. What would matter most in deciding what to do?
turns.answer_text: Keeping my word. I said I'd help, so I'd stay until it's done even if it eats my afternoon.

turns.question_text: Your current planning app is simple, offline and fine for everyday use but can't share reminders. A new one shares reminders and has better search, but switching takes about an hour and it's more complex. What would matter in deciding whether to switch?
turns.answer_text: Mainly the shared reminders. I coordinate things with my family, so that would justify the hour.

turns.question_text: Suppose a friend's move is taking much longer than you promised to help with, it's cutting into your free time, and they're fine with changing plans. What matters most to you in deciding?
turns.answer_text: My own time, really. I'd tell them I've given what I said I would and I need the rest of the day for me.

turns.question_text: You show up at a casual dinner with a few people you know. Everyone is getting things ready and nobody has assigned you anything. What catches your attention first?
turns.answer_text: I'd go find the host and ask what they need from me.

turns.question_text: You and a friend are planning a meal for just the two of you. You've offered to organise and cook it, which will take several hours, and asked your friend to buy the ingredients. They say they'd like to do the meal but paying for everything feels like too much. What would you say next?
turns.answer_text: I'd take a moment to think it over and then say something reasonable that works for both of us.

turns.question_text: You and a friend are planning a dinner for the two of you. You've offered to organise and cook it, which will take several hours, and asked them to buy the ingredients. They say they'd like to do it but buying everything feels like too much. What would you say next?
turns.answer_text: I'd say that makes sense. How about I buy the main ingredients and you bring dessert and drinks?

turns.question_text: With your basic needs covered, you unexpectedly receive about one month of your ordinary living costs, with no debt, tax or repayment attached. What would you most want that money to do for you?
turns.answer_text: I'd put it in a savings buffer so I could take a lower-paying job I'd actually like.
